。數位處理需要時間，即使只有幾毫秒，累積起來也會讓樂手覺得自己聽到的回應比動作慢: . Digital processing takes time; even a few milliseconds, added up, make players feel that the response they hear comes later than their action. If the delay is too long, players start compensating and the music runs faster and faster; if it is too short, the processing cannot produce its effect. A good part of rehearsal goes on finding this balance: which processes can tolerate delay, and which have to be immediate.
。樂手在台上聽到的，是經過混音之後的聲音，而不是樂器的原聲。如果監聽不準，樂手會: . What the players hear on stage is the mixed sound, not the acoustic sound of their instruments. If the monitoring is inaccurate, the players play at the wrong dynamic; if the monitoring is delayed, they lose their sense of time. So the monitoring design matters as much as the score, sometimes more: a bad monitor mix can make a well-prepared band sound as if it had never rehearsed.
。預錄音軌沒有呼吸，也沒有人可以看；它按自己的時間走。現場樂手要與它鎖在一起，卻: . A pre-recorded track has no breath and no one to watch; it keeps its own time. The live players have to lock to it without a shared pulse, because the track may have no clear beat. There are several common ways: one is to use a click or a guide track as the reference; two is to leave a recognisable marker sound in the track for the players to catch; three is to let the players play freely, with the track supplying only a layer of sound and no exact alignment required. These three ask completely different things of the players: the first is the steadiest but the stiffest, the third is the freest but the hardest to rehearse. A composer usually chooses one according to the nature of the music, and writes clearly in the score where the parts must line up and where they may float.
他決定哪一個聲音在前、哪一個在後、哪一個被送到哪一個喇叭、什麼時候讓回饋發生、什: He decides which sound is in front and which behind, which sound goes to which speaker, when feedback is allowed to happen and when it is pushed down. These decisions make up the work itself, rather than decorating a finished one. The same band with the same score, with a different sound engineer, can sound like two different works. This is also the most misunderstood thing about the line-up: the audience thinks it is hearing the band, when in fact it is hearing a mix the band and the sound engineer made together.
先分辨「哪個聲音是原聲、哪個是處理過的」。很多作品刻意讓兩者難以區分，這正是它的: Start by telling which sound is acoustic and which is processed. Many works deliberately make the two hard to tell apart, and that is exactly their method.
出現在當代音樂節、美術館、大學音樂廳、小型劇場與多聲道演出場地。曲目包含為樂器與: It appears at contemporary music festivals, museums, university concert halls, small theatres and multichannel venues. The repertoire includes works for instruments and fixed tracks, works for instruments and live processing, and live performances designed for a multichannel space. Lengths run from a dozen minutes to a whole evening; some works call for a particular speaker layout and have to be set up again in a new venue, so the same work can differ a great deal from one venue to the next.
即時平衡、空間化、回饋控制；是決策者，不只是技術支援: Live balance, spatialisation and feedback control; a decision maker, not just technical support
同一個處理設定在小房間與大廳聽起來完全不同，因為殘響會改變處理後聲音的密度與方向: The same processing setting sounds completely different in a small room and in a large hall, because reverb changes the density and the sense of direction of the processed sound. On tour, groups usually have to readjust the parameters at every stop rather than carry the settings over unchanged. Some works even write the characteristics of the venue into their structure, and only hold together under a particular reverb condition.
和影視配樂編制相比，差別在平衡的對象與重來的可能。配樂棚的隔離錄音是為了事後可控: Compared with the film scoring session, the difference is what the balance is for and whether anything can be done twice. Isolated recording in a scoring stage exists to keep things controllable afterwards: the balance is made at the console, the music is recorded in sections and can be started again. The electroacoustic ensemble performs live; the delays of processing and monitoring affect the players directly, the balance has to hold at that moment, and no edit can patch it later.
回饋不是單純的故障。: Feedback is not simply a fault.
因為在這個編制裡，同一個聲音會同時存在於三個地方——樂器本身、經過處理的版本、以: Because in this line-up the same sound exists in three places at once — the instrument itself, the processed version, and the space it is played into. The roles have to be divided along those three layers, or nobody knows which layer is responsible for what.
在演出當下改變聲音，不預先錄好: Changes the sound during the performance, not recorded in advance
找現場演出的錄音。這個編制的聲音設計與場地綁在一起，錄音室版本會失去空間的那一層: Look for a recording of a live performance. This line-up's sound design is tied to the venue, and a studio version loses the layer that the space provides.
把原聲轉成訊號；位置的選擇比麥克風型號更關鍵: Turns the acoustic sound into a signal; where the microphone goes matters more than which model it is
排練因此有很大一部分不在排練室。技術排練要確認訊號路徑、喇叭位置、音量與延遲，常: So a large part of rehearsal happens outside the rehearsal room. The technical rehearsal has to confirm the signal path, the speaker positions, the levels and the delay, and often takes longer than the musical rehearsal. Experienced groups separate the technical rehearsal from the musical one, getting the system stable first and only then dealing with notes and time. That also explains why touring is expensive for this line-up: the system has to be built again at every stop.
提供原聲素材，也提供演奏的身體動作: Provides the acoustic material, and the physical action of playing
提供樂手無法演奏的聲響層，或作為時間的參照: Provides sound layers the players cannot produce, or serves as a time reference
擴音會放大所有細節，包括雜音與音準偏差；延遲與監聽又讓時間控制更難。這個編制對精: Amplification magnifies every detail, including noises and intonation slips, and the delay and monitoring make control of time harder still. This line-up often demands more precision than an entirely acoustic ensemble.
最常被混為一談的是實驗聲響團體。兩者的樂器與場地大量重疊，差別在結構寫在哪裡、由: The most common confusion is with the experimental sound collective. The instruments and venues overlap heavily; the difference is where the structure is written and who decides. The experimental sound collective puts the structure into the players' judgement, using graphic scores, text scores or verbal rules to agree when to start and when to give way; the electroacoustic ensemble puts the structure into the equipment and the timeline. Fixed tracks, delay and processing parameters are themselves the frame, the sound engineer is a member, and part of the work's sound is not in the players' hands.
有電子設備就不需要準確演奏。: With electronic equipment you do not need to play accurately.
注意固定音軌什麼時候進、什麼時候退。它通常是結構的骨幹，樂手繞著它行動。: Notice when the fixed track enters and when it drops out. It is usually the backbone of the structure, and the players move around it.
注意延遲。處理後的聲音通常比原聲晚一點出現，這個時間差是編制的一部分，不是失誤。: Notice the delay. The processed sound usually appears a little later than the acoustic one; that gap is part of the line-up, not a mistake.
當麥克風收到喇叭的聲音、再放大出去，會產生回饋，頻率取決於空間與設備。在流行音樂: When a microphone picks up a speaker and the signal is amplified again, feedback occurs, at a frequency decided by the room and the equipment. In pop music this is an accident that has to be eliminated; in this line-up it can be used as material: the sound engineer can let a frequency slowly surface, hold it and push it down again. Controlling feedback requires close knowledge of the venue, because the same setting runs out of control in another room.
空間也是參數。: The space is a parameter too.
第一層是擴音。原聲樂器在音樂廳裡靠身體與空間投射，但在混合編制裡，它必須被麥克風: The first layer is amplification. In a concert hall an acoustic instrument projects through the body and the room, but in a mixed line-up it has to be caught by a microphone before it can enter the processing and the mix. Where the microphone goes decides everything: close to the instrument it catches detail, but it also catches breathing, keys and noises; further away it keeps a sense of space, but loses precision of control. The players therefore have to change how they play: not too loud, or the signal overloads, and not relying too much on the dynamics of the body, because a compressor will flatten them. For many people joining this line-up for the first time, the hardest thing is that the sound they hear is not the sound the audience hears.
第二層是即時處理。延遲、濾波、音高位移、取樣與回饋都在演出當下發生，處理後的聲音: The second layer is live processing. Delay, filtering, pitch shifting, sampling and feedback all happen during the performance, and the processed sound exists at the same time as the acoustic sound. Here there is one fact that cannot be avoided—
編制通常不大，以十人以內的中小型組合為常見，因為每一個聲部都需要獨立的麥克風與處: The line-up is usually not large, most often a mid-sized group of fewer than ten, because every part needs its own microphone and processing channel, and the more channels there are the more complicated rehearsal and performance become. The division of work is not by orchestral section but by where the sound comes from, what it passes through and where it goes.
聽空間。多聲道作品會把聲音放在觀眾四周，注意聲音從哪個方向來、怎麼移動。: Listen to the space. Multichannel works place sound all around the audience; notice which direction a sound comes from and how it moves.
與劇場音樂編制相比，差別在時間由誰驅動。劇場音樂跟著演員與舞台事件走，樂手看的是: Compared with the theatre music ensemble, the difference is what drives the time. Theatre music follows the actors and the stage events, and the players watch for cues; in the electroacoustic ensemble the time is held up by fixed tracks or by the processing structure, and the players move around that time. Stage action is not its reference.
處理後的樂器聲與固定音軌是同一層材料，會被互相混合、互相遮蔽。把它當成「樂團加伴: The processed instrument sound and the fixed track are the same layer of material, mixed with each other and masking each other. Treat it as "a band plus backing" and you will not hear that the two are in fact competing on the same plane.
設計處理方式與時間結構，通常也參與排練: Designs the processing and the time structure, and usually takes part in rehearsal
這個編制的核心是: At the heart of this line-up is—
電子原聲混合編制（Electroacoustic Ensemble）— 把原聲樂: Electroacoustic Ensemble — a hybrid line-up that amplifies and processes acoustic instruments live and keeps them in time with pre-recorded tracks; the sound engineer is one of the members. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
電子原聲混合編制（electroacoustic ensemble）是二十世紀中: The electroacoustic ensemble is a playing group that developed in European contemporary music circles from the mid-twentieth century onward: acoustic instruments are amplified through microphones and then combined with live processing and pre-recorded tracks. The problem it solves is not how to make instruments louder but how to organise acoustic instruments and electronic sound as one kind of material. So its core members are not only players but also the engineer responsible for the sound processing.
電子原聲編制就是樂團加背景音軌。: An electroacoustic ensemble is a band with a backing track.
音響師只是負責把音量調好。: The sound engineer is only there to get the levels right.
音響師因此是團員，而不是工作人員。: The sound engineer is therefore a member, not a member of staff.
音響師決定聲音的位置、層次與空間，這些決定構成作品本身。他是團員，不是技術支援。: The sound engineer decides the position, the layers and the space of the sound, and those decisions make up the work itself. He is a member, not technical support.
：把兩種本質不同的聲音放進同一個時間結構，讓它們聽起來是一件事，而不是「樂團加背: : putting two essentially different kinds of sound into one time structure so that they sound like one thing, not "a band plus a backing track".
